Heybike Shows Off V1 Pro at EICMA and It's a Promising Entry Level E-Pit Bike for the Market
9 photos
Photo: Heybike
With the appearance of electrification, the world has been flooded with ride after ride powered by nothing but near-silent and clean juice. There’s no branch of mobility or vehicle design that has gotten away either, and one that I’m currently exploring is electric mini dirt bikes or pit bikes.
Considering my re-sparked interest in motorized two-wheelers , I was able to make it out to the 2026 EICMA in Milan, a venue that stands as the largest stage for two-wheeler brands and is home to over 1,000 of them and close to 800,000 visitors over the course of six days. It was here that I witnessed the latest in electric mobility, with one crew in particular surprising me with an electric dirt bike at their stand.
Photo: Heybike Heybike is that team, a brand known for supplying the market with affordable e-bikes that can really go the distance, often seem spotted under delivery fleet service operators. So, walking by their stand at EICMA, I exclaimed when I saw that this brand has an electric pit bike in the lineup.
It’s called the V1 Pro and based on its stats and what it can do for the new rider may just make it all worth while. Then again, once we consider the price tag, it just makes sense to start your electric pit bike journey on a V1 Pro.
At it’s core, the Pro is completed with a mid-mounted motor design, and unlike a whole lot of the other entry level players out there, this motor is built around a 72 V setup, so punchy power is clearly delivered. Couple that with 250 Nm (184 lb-ft) of torque, and you can see why this one may just be worth every penny of its $2,100 price tag.
Photo: Heybike The motor peaks at a whopping 8 kw, or roughly 11 hp, so we clearly have access to ample spunk, more than enough to help us reach a top speed (limited) of 50 mph (80 kph). Ample speed if you ask me, and more than you’l probably need off-road. Currently, off-road is the only place where you can legally ride the V1 Pro.
That’s not a problem, as we can see, as Heybike also mentions that their Pro is capable of tackling hills with as much as 45 degrees inclines.
Yet, none of that means anything if range is utterly dreadful, and for the Pro, Heybike aimed pretty high. According to their website, up to 60 miles (96.5 km) of riding can be achieved with a Pro, and while the real world is sure to yield a different number, even 40-45 miles of riding seems attractive for this price and power point.
Once drained, it can take up to six hours before you’re out riding again, but from what I found out, you can purchase extra packs and double your range and ride time .
Photo: Heybike However, there’s a neat little trick up the V1 Pro’s sleeve that is sure to entice new riders, but also train them. Heybike mentions that there are four power modes in the works of the Pro, and while the first three stand for speeds, the fourth, a sort of overdrive , if you will, is to be called upon for wheelies.
All you have to do is select the fourth speed mode, hit the throttle, and the bike does the rest. There are countless brands out there these days that allow us to attain this trick, but rarely is it packed with a motor that also packs some serious heat.
In the control department, Heybike also ads a couple of extra traits that the average electric pit bike doesn’t include, one of which is the magnetic kill switch mounted to the steering wheel; if you and the bike get separated, it won’t end up in the neighbors yard before smashing into a wall.
Then there are the hydraulic brakes coupled with a hydraulic suspension at the front and rear, both of which play a part in you controlling the bike while riding, but also while catching some light airtime; the setup comes across as being able to do so. At the front, 220 mm rotors are in place, and at the rear, 190 mm.
Photo: Heybike Tires also play a crucial part in control, and on the V1 Pro , Heybike chose to add a tried and tested mullet setup, with a 17-inch wheel at the front, and a 14-inch one at the rear. The front tire rolls in with a 2.8-inch cross section while the rear offers 3.4 inches. Do enjoy the off-road ready knobs on these rubbers.
All that’s really left to do is take one of these puppies out for a spin and go from there. Keep in mind that there have already been some interest in the V1 Pro, and currently, it carries a rating of five stars out of five; there aren’t a whole lot of electric dirt bikes out there that have an unscathed rating.
